resources.string: On by default; this is the master gate for background behavior. Turning it off stops the monitoring foreground service, the heartbeat, restart-after-kill and auto-start on boot, and disables actions triggered by Tasker and the tile.

On: registers the heartbeat, auto-start on boot and restart-after-kill, and enables Tasker and the tile; the monitor only starts when auto-downgrade is enabled. Off: the monitor and heartbeat stop immediately, and there is no auto-start or restart.

The heartbeat uses the system alarm, so it may be a few minutes late while the screen is off or in battery saver. When it shows \"Stopped\", turn the switch above on to start it again; but after you tap \"Stop\" from the notification it will not be started automatically again.
On by default. On: right after writing settings, the value is read back and compared; a mismatch counts as a failure and is logged. Off: a single write is treated as success with no comparison.

Turn this off only when a write takes effect but is falsely reported as failed: some vendor ROMs read back inaccurately and mark success as failure. Once off, you have to check the system settings yourself, and failures are no longer logged.
Off by default. When on, every step of the write chain goes to the log page: which overload matched, what the modem returned, what the read-back saw, and which step threw what.

Enable only while investigating "the switch flipped but the network did not change". On the root channel diagnostics are carried back from the app_process child, so it costs extra. Turn it off once done.
The command that will actually run with the current configuration: %1$s
No value was read back (channel timed out or was denied)
Not run: no privileged channel available
Not run: could not determine the write target (the default data SIM could not be read)
Write methods available on this device

These values are probed again every time you open this page. \"Unknown\" means the value really could not be read (property unavailable, channel not authorized or timed out); it does not mean there is no problem.
This app does not branch on vendor; if a write is ignored by the system on some model, write-back verification marks it as failed and writes it to the log page, so you can look it up and pinpoint it.
